bull.t: Scaled recurring growth with strong gross margins
bull.b: The combination of substantial revenue scale and consistently high gross margins supports a durable subscription model with meaningful operating leverage potential. Continued expansion can provide increasing resources for product investment, sales capacity, and platform development while preserving strong unit economics.

Sustained positive free cash flow despite accounting losses demonstrates strong cash conversion from the subscription business and provides financial flexibility. This internally generated funding can support innovation, acquisitions, infrastructure investment, and balance-sheet management without relying solely on external capital.

bull.t: Broad platform adoption and AI security momentum
bull.b: Growth across AI protection, data security, and zero-trust deployments indicates that customers are adopting Zscaler beyond core web access. Broader platform use can increase customer value, raise cross-sell potential, and strengthen competitive positioning as security needs expand across users, workloads, branches, and AI agents.

bear.t: GAAP losses and negative shareholder returns
bear.b: Persistent GAAP losses show that the company has not yet converted its scale and gross-margin strength into sustained bottom-line profitability. Negative returns on equity can constrain the quality of earnings and keep execution dependent on continued growth, disciplined spending, and eventual operating leverage.

A shift from mid-20s growth to mid-teens growth would slow the pace at which Zscaler expands its recurring revenue base. Lower growth can reduce operating leverage and make execution more important, particularly as the company invests in AI-focused offerings and broadens beyond its traditional user-based model.

bear.t: Sales leadership turnover creates execution risk
bear.b: Sales leadership changes can disrupt account coverage, forecasting, hiring, and large-deal execution during a period when growth expectations are already moderating. Even with internal and external replacements underway, transition risk may temporarily affect new-logo acquisition, productivity, and the consistency of expansion bookings.
